techniques.semanticProblem: A spoken hook contains several pressure points that need one escalating visual sentence.
useWhen: phrase timing is clear
presenter remains the visual anchor
avoidWhen: every word would become a separate effect
the face would become unreadable
techniques.motionGrammar: hidden phrase groups below their final baseline -> groups rise on speech pressure with unequal timing -> two stable lines hold as one hero statement

techniques.semanticProblem: Many tools must feel like accumulated input rather than a screenshot wall.
useWhen: multiple real assets share one concept
the operator remains the center of causality
avoidWhen: the assets are not real
the tableau would cover the presenter without adding evidence
techniques.motionGrammar: clean presenter frame -> paired evidence cards approach a central operator in depth -> the tableau lands with one readable center and balanced sides

techniques.semanticProblem: A noun phrase needs emphasis without becoming another hero title.
techniques.motionGrammar: phrase absent beside existing evidence -> phrase travels a short horizontal path while resolving opacity -> phrase lands beside the evidence and leaves before the next idea

techniques.semanticProblem: A reflective sentence needs visual emphasis without kinetic noise.
techniques.motionGrammar: clean A-roll -> one phrase resolves from soft opacity with almost no travel -> phrase holds briefly while the presenter remains dominant

techniques.semanticProblem: A move into coding should feel like entering an executable system, not turning to a slide.
techniques.motionGrammar: presenter stage is still visible -> a code window opens through a directional mask and internal lines resolve in order -> a complete executable-looking system holds with the term anchored above it

techniques.semanticProblem: Real material must become the argument without losing orientation.
techniques.motionGrammar: full-frame evidence establishes -> camera makes one restrained push toward the relevant subject -> source identity and focal evidence remain readable at the landing

techniques.semanticProblem: Several examples must converge into a single claimed result.
techniques.motionGrammar: evidence is outside the composition -> three real cards open from one compressed center with depth separation -> the cards land as one row and the result phrase receives one final mark

techniques.semanticProblem: A factual claim names a person, message, document, product, or action and the audience needs to see the matching evidence at the exact spoken cue.
useWhen: the material is authentic and legible
the spoken cue has a clear entry and exit
avoidWhen: the asset only decorates the topic
the evidence would appear before the audience knows what to inspect
techniques.motionGrammar: presenter establishes the claim -> matching evidence takes over on the named cue -> evidence holds long enough to read -> attention returns to the presenter or hands off to the next proof

review.evidence: The user retained the real-evidence word handoff in the approved final edit.

techniques.semanticProblem: Real footage must first be understood in full and then remain present while the narration returns to the presenter.
useWhen: the evidence needs full-frame establishment
the same evidence still matters after the presenter returns
avoidWhen: the inset would cover a face or caption
the evidence is too small to remain meaningful as PIP
techniques.motionGrammar: evidence fills the frame and establishes -> the same uncropped evidence shrinks with a long-tail ease into a face-safe rounded PIP -> presenter resumes while the inset completes the thought

review.evidence: The user retained the full-frame evidence to PIP handoff in the approved final edit.

techniques.semanticProblem: Several real examples must register as accumulated proof without stopping the narration for a screenshot wall.
useWhen: each source is recognizable at short duration
the sequence supports one spoken claim
avoidWhen: the audience must read dense copy
the sources do not share one argument
techniques.motionGrammar: presenter or first proof establishes -> real sources replace one another on speech beats with consistent focal placement -> the final source lands long enough to hand off the conclusion

techniques.semanticProblem: Several pages or cases must feel like a body of work growing around a presenter rather than flat cards pasted over the frame.
useWhen: the presenter is the causal center
the pages can remain recognizable at an angle
avoidWhen: the cards would obscure the presenters
the layout has no shared pivot or depth hierarchy
techniques.motionGrammar: presenter remains centered -> pages emerge from one hidden pivot behind the body -> left and right pages fan outward with different perspective angles and depth -> the spread settles as one readable spatial relationship

review.evidence: The user repeatedly defined the person-centered flower-like fan and retained the corrected spatial method.

techniques.semanticProblem: An abstract claim needs a concrete, playful, human-scale explanation that real footage cannot show directly.
useWhen: the scene can show a readable setup, action, and result
generated characters or objects are explanatory rather than factual evidence
avoidWhen: one static generated composition would be treated as motion
the same pose or scene would be repeated across unrelated claims
techniques.motionGrammar: generate content-specific people, objects, and backgrounds as separable assets -> key, complete, and layer the pieces -> animate a clear setup, action, reaction, and result -> exit back to the presenter or evidence on the spoken handoff

review.evidence: The user repeatedly required ImageGen-built, cutout, completed, and animated Vox scenes using the two creators' likenesses.

techniques.semanticProblem: A chapter change needs a calm black spatial bridge that suggests terrain, pressure, hierarchy, or a path without becoming a slide.
useWhen: the chapter has a terrain, growth, complexity, or systems metaphor
the transition can breathe for roughly one second
avoidWhen: random lines would add no meaning
the field would be cropped, dashed, or move too quickly
techniques.motionGrammar: black field replaces the outgoing shot -> complete contour paths draw and drift slowly beyond the frame edges -> chapter text resolves after the terrain exists -> the field hands off and exits

review.evidence: The user retained the black moving contour transition after correcting speed and edge continuity.

techniques.semanticProblem: A chapter change about networks, collaboration, systems, or AI nodes needs a structured black transition rather than decoration over the presenter.
useWhen: nodes or relationships are semantically relevant
the field exists only for the transition
avoidWhen: dots would remain over the dialogue scene
points or lines would be arbitrary decoration
techniques.motionGrammar: black field takes over -> points drift into a deliberate arrangement -> only meaningful links illuminate -> chapter copy appears after the relationship is readable -> the entire field exits before dialogue resumes

review.evidence: The user explicitly retained the point-field idea as a transition-only technique.

techniques.semanticProblem: A system story must show scattered knowledge becoming organized and reusable without switching to a disconnected presentation slide.
useWhen: the same real materials recur across several stages
the narration describes capture, organization, and reuse
avoidWhen: the materials do not persist across the story
the transformation would be decorative rather than causal
techniques.motionGrammar: real materials appear in their original scattered carriers -> the same items move into one visible index -> the index retrieves the relevant item on cue -> the retrieved material becomes the next action or output

review.evidence: The user retained the scatter-to-index-to-retrieve visual spine in the approved final edit.

techniques.semanticProblem: A spoken emphasis needs a spatial change that feels intentional rather than a temporary zoom effect.
useWhen: the face, gesture, or evidence has a clear landing frame
the scale change shares one semantic beat with display type or sound
avoidWhen: the crop would lose a face, hand, subtitle, or proof
the move would bounce back without a new spoken reason
techniques.motionGrammar: current framing -> fast-starting scale and position change with a long deceleration tail -> new framing lands and remains fixed until another independent cue

review.evidence: The user repeatedly retained fast-to-slow push and pull moves only when they land and hold.

techniques.semanticProblem: A short hook needs large editorial hierarchy while the presenter remains continuously visible.
useWhen: the copy can be reduced to a few horizontal display phrases
subject edges are stable enough for foreground and background type
avoidWhen: the words would cover the eyes, mouth, or essential gesture
ordinary bilingual captions are being mistaken for hook typography
techniques.motionGrammar: presenter remains full-frame -> one display phrase establishes a foreground or background plane -> the presenter occludes part of a larger phrase -> later words replace or defocus the previous layer without vertical text

review.evidence: The user retained the layered horizontal hook typography in the approved final edit.

techniques.semanticProblem: The opening must reject the obvious answer and reveal the true subject within the first three seconds.
useWhen: the hook contains one short counterclaim and one clear reveal
the presenter can remain the visual anchor
avoidWhen: the argument needs a long setup
the true claim cannot be read around the subject
techniques.motionGrammar: extreme or tight presenter frame with the expected answer -> long-tail pull-back and defocus demote that answer -> the true claim expands behind or around the presenter and lands with a separately licensed outward whoosh

review.evidence: The user explicitly approved the visual and sound relationship. The original audio master is intentionally not bundled.

techniques.semanticProblem: A digital chapter change needs visible assembly or reset without becoming a presentation slide.
useWhen: the topic supports a digital, system, or reconstruction metaphor
the pixel field can resolve into the incoming scene
avoidWhen: the same effect already appeared at an adjacent boundary
pixelation has no relationship to either scene
techniques.motionGrammar: outgoing image breaks into controlled cells -> cells reorganize across a black or scene-derived field -> incoming scene resolves and holds cleanly

review.evidence: The user repeatedly retained pixel-style chapter transitions when they supported the topic.
